title: Amazon EventBridge: Event Buses, Pipes & Scheduler
summary: Route events between services and SaaS apps, connect sources to targets, and run schedules.
tldr: **Event bus + rules**: many producers, many consumers. Rules match on event content (including numeric ranges and prefixes) and route to targets. SaaS partners deliver straight to a **partner event bus**, and AWS services publish to the **default bus**.
**Pipes**: one source to one target, with optional **filter**, **enrichment** and transformation in between. It replaces glue code that polls SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, Amazon MQ or Kafka.
**Scheduler**: cron, rate and **one-time** schedules for millions of tasks, with time zones, retries and a DLQ. It's the answer for "run X at time T" without polling a database.

keyFacts.text: Maximum targets on one rule (fixed). Need more consumers? Add more rules on the same bus, each matching the same pattern.
An **archive** keeps matching bus events for the days you set (indefinitely by default). A **replay** re-sends a time window to the source bus.
Turn on EventBridge for a bucket and every S3 event goes to the default bus. Then add a rule per consumer instead of overlapping S3 notifications.
Scheduler and rule targets support a **retry policy** (maximum event age, retry attempts) and an **SQS dead-letter queue** for events that still fail.
An SQS delay queue or message timer can postpone delivery by at most 15 minutes. Longer delays (hours, days) call for **Scheduler one-time schedules**.

traps: Two S3 event notification configurations can't overlap on the same event type and prefix. Use EventBridge to fan out.
An EventBridge rule can't match "a message arriving in an SQS queue". Reading from a queue is a job for Pipes or a Lambda event source mapping.
DynamoDB TTL deletes items on a best-effort schedule, not at an exact time, so it is a poor timer.
A rule that runs every minute and scans a database is the polling design the question wants you to avoid.
SNS subscription filter policies filter messages, but SNS can't poll an SQS queue or enrich a message.
Rules on a classic event bus don't guarantee delivery order; ordered fan-out is an SNS FIFO job.
